prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Photo Quality Tips", "Ensure good lighting and a clear face view for the best custom pet results.", "Continue"]
1: ["Logging back in? Use the same account you used before to keep your pet and progress safe."]
2: ["How Your Pet Lives On Desktop", "Preview feeding, playing, and desktop interactions before finalizing your companion.", "Looks Good"]
3: ["Sign In to Save Pet", "Secure authentication is connecting to save your pet online."]
4: ["Upload Pet Photos", "Select clear photos of your pet from different angles for best results."]
5: ["Choose Your Pet's Journey", "Select whether to pick from pre-made pet friends or create a custom pet companion."]
6: ["Preparing Desktop Pet", "Setting up animations, sound effects, and desktop interactions."]
7: ["Your Pet is Ready!", "Click your pet anytime to interact, right-click for settings, or drag to reposition on your desktop."]
8: ["Try Interacting With Your Pet", "Click and drag to see how your pet responds on screen.", "Adopt This Pet"]
9: ["Setup takes only 2 minutes. Your pet will live right on your desktop!"]
